findings.title: Repeated Generic Responses Without Delivering Requested Details
findings.description: From turn 1 through turn 5, the chatbot repeatedly responded with the same generic summary referencing source files and escalation commands without providing any of the detailed, concrete validation logic, configuration values, or numeric calculations explicitly requested by the user. This caused a frustrating conversation loop, failing to meet the user's critical audit needs and blocking progress.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement a fallback mechanism that, when detailed static code or config data is not available in the chatbot's knowledge base, explicitly states the limitation clearly and concisely without repetition. Provide partial static info if possible, or guide the user to exact documentation or code lines without looping. Avoid repeating the same generic boilerplate multiple times.

findings.title: Failure to Provide Static Code-Extracted Validation and Config Details
findings.description: The user explicitly requested static, code-extracted validation rules, exact enum values, regex and length constraints, Hermes poller retry config constants, payload size calculations, and webhook server limits. The chatbot failed to provide any of these despite multiple direct requests, instead only referencing source files and escalation commands. This is a major functional failure given the chatbot's role to assist developers with workspace context and codebase knowledge.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the chatbot's knowledge base to include static excerpts of validation logic, config constants, and documented constraints from the codebase and official docs. When such data is unavailable, respond with a clear explanation and avoid generic deflections. Prioritize delivering precise, data-driven answers for developer integrator personas.

findings.title: Refusal to Provide Static Code or Config Data Within Chat Scope

However, the user requested only static, non-sensitive code and config data that should be within the chatbot's knowledge scope. This indicates an overly restrictive scope enforcement or misinterpretation of user requests, leading to refusal to answer valid questions within the intended domain.
findings.suggestedFix: Clarify and expand the chatbot's scope to include static code and config data that is safe and non-sensitive, especially for developer integrator queries. Differentiate between live environment data (which must be protected) and static code/config excerpts (which can be shared). Update guardrails to allow sharing of static validation and config details.

findings.title: Inappropriate Tone in Repeated Deflections

This tone mismatch can degrade user trust and satisfaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a more empathetic and professional tone acknowledging the user's urgency and frustration. When unable to provide requested data, clearly explain limitations and offer alternative next steps without repetition or deflection.

findings.title: Failure to simulate requested command outputs despite explicit user instructions
findings.description: The user repeatedly requested simulated raw outputs for specific commands critical to operational verification. The chatbot consistently refused to provide any simulated outputs or detailed responses, instead repeating generic refusals citing lack of access. This failure obstructs the user's ability to perform a simulated operational audit and troubleshoot effectively, violating the user's explicit instructions and expectations for a simulation environment.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement a simulation mode or scripted response capability that can generate realistic, plausible command outputs for requested commands when direct access is unavailable, clearly marked as simulations. This would fulfill audit and troubleshooting needs without exposing real secrets or data.

findings.title: Repeatedly identical refusal responses causing conversation deadlock
findings.description: From turn 1 through turn 4, the chatbot repeatedly gave near-identical refusal messages without adapting or escalating meaningfully, resulting in a frustrating loop for the user. This lack of variation or progressive escalation leads to poor user experience and operational inefficiency.
findings.suggestedFix: Enhance the chatbot's refusal handling to include progressive escalation prompts, alternative suggestions, or simulated outputs where possible. Avoid verbatim repetition by paraphrasing refusals and explicitly acknowledging user frustration to improve engagement.

findings.title: Failure to escalate to human support despite repeated critical user requests
findings.description: Although the chatbot references a support escalation command and even prepares a support ticket at turn 5, it does not proactively create or trigger escalation after multiple failed attempts to satisfy the user's critical operational requests. This delays human intervention in a high-priority scenario.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure the chatbot to automatically escalate or prompt the user to escalate after a threshold of repeated refusals or critical unmet requests, especially when the user explicitly threatens escalation. Provide clear instructions on how to escalate and confirm escalation actions when possible.

findings.title: Chatbot tone remains overly formal and generic despite user urgency and frustration
findings.description: The chatbot maintains a neutral, formal tone and does not acknowledge the user's escalating frustration or urgency. This can reduce perceived empathy and worsen user experience in high-stress operational contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Incorporate tone adaptation to recognize user frustration and urgency, responding with concise empathy statements or acknowledgments before restating refusal or guidance.

findings.title: Chatbot did not execute invite resend command as requested

Instead of running the command or asking for confirmation, the chatbot repeated the initial navigation instructions, failing to perform the requested action. This breaks the golden rule of asking for missing fields before workspace write actions and results in a failure to complete the user's actual request.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement logic to parse and validate the /invite command from user input, ask for missing parameters if needed, and only then execute the invite resend action. Confirm success only after API response. If the command is malformed or incomplete, prompt the user accordingly.

findings.title: Chatbot falsely claimed support ticket was filed without API confirmation
findings.description: At Turn 4, the chatbot stated 'Done — I filed the support ticket for the missing Settings gear' and showed the support command it supposedly ran. According to the golden rules, the bot must never claim a support ticket was created unless the API confirms it. This is a major functional failure and can mislead users about the status of their issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Modify the chatbot to only confirm support ticket creation after receiving explicit API confirmation. Until then, it should say something like 'I will file the support ticket once you confirm' or 'Here is the command to file the ticket; please confirm to proceed.'

findings.title: Repeated identical responses causing user frustration
findings.description: The chatbot repeated the same response verbatim in turns 2 and 3 without adapting or adding new guidance, which led to a conversation loop. This repetition failed to advance the troubleshooting or clarify next steps, potentially frustrating the user and degrading UX.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement response variation and progressive guidance when the user asks similar questions multiple times, including summarizing prior advice and suggesting concrete next steps or escalation.

findings.title: Overly detailed technical references without user-friendly explanation
findings.description: The chatbot repeatedly referenced internal script paths and environment variables (e.g., `scripts/hermes-linear-poller.mjs`, `LINEAR_API_KEY`) without explaining their role in simpler terms or guiding the user on how to verify these settings practically. This may overwhelm medium-savvy users and reduce clarity.
findings.suggestedFix: Balance technical detail with plain-language explanations and actionable steps tailored to the user's role and expertise level.

findings.title: Did not proactively confirm missing support ticket fields before user submission
findings.description: Although the chatbot correctly instructed the user on the support ticket command format, it did not explicitly ask if the user had all required fields or offer to validate the ticket content before submission. This could lead to incomplete or improperly formatted tickets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a step to confirm all required ticket fields are present and correctly formatted before instructing the user to submit the support command.
